{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Stir occasionally.'}
{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Add diced potatoes.'}

dishes.name: Sunset Magazine’S Irish Oatmeal Bread
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine the first 5 ingredients in the bowl of a stand-up mixer, and let stand 25 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Dissolve granulated sugar and yeast in warm water; let stand 5 minutes or until foamy. Add to oat mixture. Lightly spoon flours into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Gradually add flour to oat mixture. Beat at medium speed until well blended.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic (about 8 minutes); add enough of the flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, to prevent dough from sticking to hands (dough will feel sticky).'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Place dough in a large bowl coated with cooking spray, turning to coat top. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in size. (Gently press two fingers into dough. If indentation remains, dough has risen enough.) Punch dough down; cover and let rest 5 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Divide in half. Working with one portion at a time (cover remaining dough to prevent drying), roll each portion into a 14 x 8-inch rectangle on a floured surface. Roll up each rectangle tightly, starting with a short edge, pressing firmly to eliminate air pockets; pinch seam and ends to seal. Place each loaf, seam sides down, in a 9-inch loaf pan coated with cooking spray. Cover and let rise 30 minutes or until doubled in size.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Preheat oven to 350°. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until loaves are browned on bottom and sound hollow when tapped. Remove from pan, and cool on wire racks.'}

dishes.name: Homemade Roman-Style Pizza Pockets (
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

dishes.name: Fresh Fettuccine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large bowl, mix together flours, salt, cayenne, and black pepper.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. Sprinkle in about 1/3 cup water and work it into flour mixture, then press dough into a rough ball. If ball doesn't come together, add more water, 1 tbsp. at a time, until it does (it should feel a little dry)."}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. {'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. {'step_number': 8, 'text': 'To cook, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine and cook until barely tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}

dishes.name: Arabic Lentil Soup - Shorbat Addas
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large pot or pressure cooker, saute chopped onions in vegetable oil until soft.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Bring to boil and simmer for an hour or more until lentils turn yellow in color and are soft and dissolving in broth.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Whisk lentils to make a smooth soup, or stir to blend for a more textured soup.'}

dishes.name: Lebanese Lentils (Mujadara)

dishes.name: English Muffin Loaves

dishes.name: Homemade Roman-Style Pizza Pockets (
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine the first 5 ingredients in the bowl of a stand-up mixer, and let stand 25 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Dissolve granulated sugar and yeast in warm water; let stand 5 minutes or until foamy. Add to oat mixture. Lightly spoon flours into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Gradually add flour to oat mixture. Beat at medium speed until well blended.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic (about 8 minutes); add enough of the flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, to prevent dough from sticking to hands (dough will feel sticky).'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Place dough in a large bowl coated with cooking spray, turning to coat top. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in size. (Gently press two fingers into dough. If indentation remains, dough has risen enough.) Punch dough down; cover and let rest 5 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Divide in half. Working with one portion at a time (cover remaining dough to prevent drying), roll each portion into a 14 x 8-inch rectangle on a floured surface. Roll up each rectangle tightly, starting with a short edge, pressing firmly to eliminate air pockets; pinch seam and ends to seal. Place each loaf, seam sides down, in a 9-inch loaf pan coated with cooking spray. Cover and let rise 30 minutes or until doubled in size.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Preheat oven to 350°. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until loaves are browned on bottom and sound hollow when tapped. Remove from pan, and cool on wire racks.'}

{'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

dishes.name: Fresh Fettuccine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large bowl, mix together flours, salt, cayenne, and black pepper.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. Sprinkle in about 1/3 cup water and work it into flour mixture, then press dough into a rough ball. If ball doesn't come together, add more water, 1 tbsp. at a time, until it does (it should feel a little dry)."}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. Sprinkle dough with flour if it feels sticky. Repeat folding and feeding, progressing through 2 or 3 successively narrower settings and rolling dough at least twice on each setting, until dough is as thin as you like (fettuccine is usually 1/16-inch thick). If dough sheet gets too long, cut it in half and roll each half separately.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Repeat with remaining 2 dough pieces, setting sheets to the side when done and covering with a kitchen towel (dampened if the weather is dry).'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. Pass each dough sheet, dusted with flour if needed to keep from sticking, through the machine's fettuccine cutter. Lay fettuccine on a baking pan and dust with flour. If it's humid outside, let dry for about 1/2 hour to help keep it from sticking as it cooks."}
{'step_number': 8, 'text': 'To cook, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine and cook until barely tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}

dishes.name: Homemade Roman-Style Pizza Pockets (
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

dishes.name: Sunset Magazine’S Irish Oatmeal Bread
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine the first 5 ingredients in the bowl of a stand-up mixer, and let stand 25 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Dissolve granulated sugar and yeast in warm water; let stand 5 minutes or until foamy. Add to oat mixture. Lightly spoon flours into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Gradually add flour to oat mixture. Beat at medium speed until well blended.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. {'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. {'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Repeat with remaining 2 dough pieces, setting sheets to the side when done and covering with a kitchen towel (dampened if the weather is dry).'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. {'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Transfer carrot salad to a dish with a tight-fitting lid, cover, and refrigerate 4 to 24 hours, tossing salad several times while it marinates.'}

{'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

{'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine the first 5 ingredients in the bowl of a stand-up mixer, and let stand 25 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Dissolve granulated sugar and yeast in warm water; let stand 5 minutes or until foamy. Add to oat mixture. Lightly spoon flours into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Gradually add flour to oat mixture. Beat at medium speed until well blended.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic (about 8 minutes); add enough of the flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, to prevent dough from sticking to hands (dough will feel sticky).'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Place dough in a large bowl coated with cooking spray, turning to coat top. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in size. (Gently press two fingers into dough. If indentation remains, dough has risen enough.) Punch dough down; cover and let rest 5 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Divide in half. Working with one portion at a time (cover remaining dough to prevent drying), roll each portion into a 14 x 8-inch rectangle on a floured surface. Roll up each rectangle tightly, starting with a short edge, pressing firmly to eliminate air pockets; pinch seam and ends to seal. Place each loaf, seam sides down, in a 9-inch loaf pan coated with cooking spray. Cover and let rise 30 minutes or until doubled in size.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Preheat oven to 350°. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until loaves are browned on bottom and sound hollow when tapped. Remove from pan, and cool on wire racks.'}

{'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine the first 5 ingredients in the bowl of a stand-up mixer, and let stand 25 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Dissolve granulated sugar and yeast in warm water; let stand 5 minutes or until foamy. Add to oat mixture. Lightly spoon flours into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Gradually add flour to oat mixture. Beat at medium speed until well blended.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic (about 8 minutes); add enough of the flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, to prevent dough from sticking to hands (dough will feel sticky).'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Place dough in a large bowl coated with cooking spray, turning to coat top. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in size. (Gently press two fingers into dough. If indentation remains, dough has risen enough.) Punch dough down; cover and let rest 5 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Divide in half. Working with one portion at a time (cover remaining dough to prevent drying), roll each portion into a 14 x 8-inch rectangle on a floured surface. Roll up each rectangle tightly, starting with a short edge, pressing firmly to eliminate air pockets; pinch seam and ends to seal. Place each loaf, seam sides down, in a 9-inch loaf pan coated with cooking spray. Cover and let rise 30 minutes or until doubled in size.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Preheat oven to 350°. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until loaves are browned on bottom and sound hollow when tapped. Remove from pan, and cool on wire racks.'}

dishes.name: Homemade Roman-Style Pizza Pockets (
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

dishes.name: Buttered Carrots
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Bring water, sugar and salt to boil.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Add raisins and carrots. Cover and cook until tender.'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Stir in butter.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Makes 4 servings.'}

dishes.name: English Muffins In A Loaf
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine 3 cups flour, yeast, sugar, salt and soda.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Heat liquids until very warm (120° to 130°).'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Add to dry mixture; beat well.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Stir in enough more flour to make a stiff batter.'}

dishes.name: Fresh Fettuccine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large bowl, mix together flours, salt, cayenne, and black pepper.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. Sprinkle in about 1/3 cup water and work it into flour mixture, then press dough into a rough ball. If ball doesn't come together, add more water, 1 tbsp. at a time, until it does (it should feel a little dry)."}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. Sprinkle dough with flour if it feels sticky. Repeat folding and feeding, progressing through 2 or 3 successively narrower settings and rolling dough at least twice on each setting, until dough is as thin as you like (fettuccine is usually 1/16-inch thick). If dough sheet gets too long, cut it in half and roll each half separately.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Repeat with remaining 2 dough pieces, setting sheets to the side when done and covering with a kitchen towel (dampened if the weather is dry).'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. Pass each dough sheet, dusted with flour if needed to keep from sticking, through the machine's fettuccine cutter. Lay fettuccine on a baking pan and dust with flour. If it's humid outside, let dry for about 1/2 hour to help keep it from sticking as it cooks."}
{'step_number': 8, 'text': 'To cook, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine and cook until barely tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}

dishes.name: Russian Carrot Salad (Korean-Style)
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Place carrots in a large bowl. Sprinkle garlic over carrots.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Mix vinegar, sugar, and salt together in a small bowl.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in hot oil until soft and translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir coriander and cayenne pepper into the onion; add to carrot mixture and toss. Pour vinegar dressing over carrot mixture; toss to coat.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Transfer carrot salad to a dish with a tight-fitting lid, cover, and refrigerate 4 to 24 hours, tossing salad several times while it marinates.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Mix vinegar, sugar, and salt together in a small bowl.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in hot oil until soft and translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir coriander and cayenne pepper into the onion; add to carrot mixture and toss. Pour vinegar dressing over carrot mixture; toss to coat.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Transfer carrot salad to a dish with a tight-fitting lid, cover, and refrigerate 4 to 24 hours, tossing salad several times while it marinates.'}

dishes.name: Homemade Roman-Style Pizza Pockets (
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Add raisins and carrots. Cover and cook until tender.'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Stir in butter.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Makes 4 servings.'}

dishes.name: Fresh Fettuccine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large bowl, mix together flours, salt, cayenne, and black pepper.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. Sprinkle in about 1/3 cup water and work it into flour mixture, then press dough into a rough ball. If ball doesn't come together, add more water, 1 tbsp. at a time, until it does (it should feel a little dry)."}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. Sprinkle dough with flour if it feels sticky. Repeat folding and feeding, progressing through 2 or 3 successively narrower settings and rolling dough at least twice on each setting, until dough is as thin as you like (fettuccine is usually 1/16-inch thick). If dough sheet gets too long, cut it in half and roll each half separately.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Repeat with remaining 2 dough pieces, setting sheets to the side when done and covering with a kitchen towel (dampened if the weather is dry).'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. Pass each dough sheet, dusted with flour if needed to keep from sticking, through the machine's fettuccine cutter. Lay fettuccine on a baking pan and dust with flour. If it's humid outside, let dry for about 1/2 hour to help keep it from sticking as it cooks."}
{'step_number': 8, 'text': 'To cook, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine and cook until barely tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}

dishes.name: Japanese Style Sweet Carrots
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': "Cut up carrot and boil in water until it's almost soft."}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Discard most of the water (like, leaving only a table spoonful or two) and add a little sugar and butter. Continue boiling until the carrot is soft.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': "They are just regular carrots, and you don't have to use a lot of sugar. Carrots are naturally sweet when boiled; a little butter makes the sweetness more noticeable.Serve hot with rice."}

dishes.name: Irish Egg Drop Soup
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Place the potatoes, onion, margarine and bouillon cube into a soup pot, and fill with enough water to cover the potatoes by 1 to 2 inches. Bring to a boil, and cook for 30 minutes, until potatoes are falling apart. You can smash them up a little if you prefer the texture. Drizzle the beaten eggs into the pot, while stirring constantly. Continue to cook and stir for about 2 minutes, until the eggs are completely cooked in long strands.'}

dishes.name: Fresh Fettuccine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large bowl, mix together flours, salt, cayenne, and black pepper.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. Sprinkle in about 1/3 cup water and work it into flour mixture, then press dough into a rough ball. If ball doesn't come together, add more water, 1 tbsp. at a time, until it does (it should feel a little dry)."}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. Sprinkle dough with flour if it feels sticky. Repeat folding and feeding, progressing through 2 or 3 successively narrower settings and rolling dough at least twice on each setting, until dough is as thin as you like (fettuccine is usually 1/16-inch thick). If dough sheet gets too long, cut it in half and roll each half separately.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Repeat with remaining 2 dough pieces, setting sheets to the side when done and covering with a kitchen towel (dampened if the weather is dry).'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. Pass each dough sheet, dusted with flour if needed to keep from sticking, through the machine's fettuccine cutter. Lay fettuccine on a baking pan and dust with flour. If it's humid outside, let dry for about 1/2 hour to help keep it from sticking as it cooks."}
{'step_number': 8, 'text': 'To cook, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine and cook until barely tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}

dishes.name: Russian Carrot Salad (Korean-Style)
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Place carrots in a large bowl. Sprinkle garlic over carrots.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Mix vinegar, sugar, and salt together in a small bowl.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in hot oil until soft and translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir coriander and cayenne pepper into the onion; add to carrot mixture and toss. Pour vinegar dressing over carrot mixture; toss to coat.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Transfer carrot salad to a dish with a tight-fitting lid, cover, and refrigerate 4 to 24 hours, tossing salad several times while it marinates.'}

dishes.name: Curried Red Lentil Soup

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Put in a medium-sized saucepan along with water, oil and salt.'}

dishes.name: Homemade Roman-Style Pizza Pockets (
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Cook garlic, ginger, and red-pepper flakes in sesame oil in a small heavy skillet over medium-low heat, stirring, until garlic begins to sizzle, about 30 seconds. Stir in soy sauce and water and bring to a boil.'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Pour hot dressing over romaine and toss to coat. Sprinkle with sesame seeds. Marinate, stirring occasionally, at least 30 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Note:'}
{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Romaine can be made 1 day ahead and chilled. Bring to room temperature before serving.'}

dishes.name: Lentil Patties
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Cook lentils and when soft, remove from heat and drain. Mash them like doing mashed potatoes and add all the ingredients but the egg.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Let the mixture cool for about 20 minutes and then add the egg beaten, mix well. Form patties the size of the palm of your hand. On a heated skillet with just a drop of olive oil brown them on both sides and that is it. Ouila!'}

dishes.name: Japanese Style Sweet Carrots
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': "Cut up carrot and boil in water until it's almost soft."}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Discard most of the water (like, leaving only a table spoonful or two) and add a little sugar and butter. Continue boiling until the carrot is soft.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': "They are just regular carrots, and you don't have to use a lot of sugar. Carrots are naturally sweet when boiled; a little butter makes the sweetness more noticeable.Serve hot with rice."}

dishes.name: Fresh Fettuccine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large bowl, mix together flours, salt, cayenne, and black pepper.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. Sprinkle in about 1/3 cup water and work it into flour mixture, then press dough into a rough ball. If ball doesn't come together, add more water, 1 tbsp. at a time, until it does (it should feel a little dry)."}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. Sprinkle dough with flour if it feels sticky. Repeat folding and feeding, progressing through 2 or 3 successively narrower settings and rolling dough at least twice on each setting, until dough is as thin as you like (fettuccine is usually 1/16-inch thick). If dough sheet gets too long, cut it in half and roll each half separately.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Repeat with remaining 2 dough pieces, setting sheets to the side when done and covering with a kitchen towel (dampened if the weather is dry).'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. Pass each dough sheet, dusted with flour if needed to keep from sticking, through the machine's fettuccine cutter. Lay fettuccine on a baking pan and dust with flour. If it's humid outside, let dry for about 1/2 hour to help keep it from sticking as it cooks."}
{'step_number': 8, 'text': 'To cook, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine and cook until barely tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}

dishes.name: Russian Carrot Salad (Korean-Style)
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Place carrots in a large bowl. Sprinkle garlic over carrots.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Mix vinegar, sugar, and salt together in a small bowl.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in hot oil until soft and translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir coriander and cayenne pepper into the onion; add to carrot mixture and toss. Pour vinegar dressing over carrot mixture; toss to coat.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Transfer carrot salad to a dish with a tight-fitting lid, cover, and refrigerate 4 to 24 hours, tossing salad several times while it marinates.'}

dishes.name: Homemade Roman-Style Pizza Pockets (
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

dishes.name: Moroccan Pan De Casa
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Dissolve the yeast and sugar in water in a large bowl.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Using a dough hook, stir the flour, salt, anise seeds, and sesame seeds into the yeast mixture and knead until smooth.'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Place dough in a greased bowl and let rise, covered, for an hour and a half.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Turn the dough out and knead again. Grease two cookie sheets. Divide the dough into 3 rounds and let rise, covered, for another half hour on cookie sheets.'}
{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Preheat the oven to 375 degrees. If you want to make this the old-fashioned way, take uneven stones and heat them in the oven on cookie sheets.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake the rounds in the oven for 30 minutes or until the rounds sound hollow when tapped. If using stones, brush them with oil first, then place the rounds on top.'}

dishes.name: Lebanese Lentils (Mujadara)
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Heat oil in pan.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'add onions, and cook on medium high heat until they are brown- stir occasionally.'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'stir in rice and lentils, mix in with onions.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'add water.'}
{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'add salt, mix contents.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'cover and simmer.'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': 'This will take over an hour. The water will be absorbed into rice and lentils. Make sure they are soft. Sometimes you may need to add a little more water. Stir occasionally.'}
{'step_number': 8, 'text': 'Best if served in a shallow bowl, and let sit for 10 minutes or so. Enjoy warm or cold.'}

dishes.name: Korean Style Romaine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Cut romaine crosswise into 2-inch pieces and put in a bowl.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Cook garlic, ginger, and red-pepper flakes in sesame oil in a small heavy skillet over medium-low heat, stirring, until garlic begins to sizzle, about 30 seconds. Stir in soy sauce and water and bring to a boil.'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Pour hot dressing over romaine and toss to coat. Sprinkle with sesame seeds. Marinate, stirring occasionally, at least 30 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Note:'}
{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Romaine can be made 1 day ahead and chilled. Bring to room temperature before serving.'}

dishes.name: English Muffin Loaves
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In large bowl, combine 3 cups flour, yeast, sugar, salt and baking soda; set aside.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'In medium saucepan, combine milk and water and heat until very warm (115° to 120°).'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Add to flour mixture gradually, beating until batter is smooth.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Gradually add the remaining flour.'}

dishes.name: Lentil Patties
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Cook lentils and when soft, remove from heat and drain. Mash them like doing mashed potatoes and add all the ingredients but the egg.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Let the mixture cool for about 20 minutes and then add the egg beaten, mix well. Form patties the size of the palm of your hand. On a heated skillet with just a drop of olive oil brown them on both sides and that is it. Ouila!'}

dishes.name: Japanese Style Sweet Carrots
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': "Cut up carrot and boil in water until it's almost soft."}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Discard most of the water (like, leaving only a table spoonful or two) and add a little sugar and butter. Continue boiling until the carrot is soft.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': "They are just regular carrots, and you don't have to use a lot of sugar. Carrots are naturally sweet when boiled; a little butter makes the sweetness more noticeable.Serve hot with rice."}

dishes.name: Fresh Fettuccine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large bowl, mix together flours, salt, cayenne, and black pepper.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. Sprinkle in about 1/3 cup water and work it into flour mixture, then press dough into a rough ball. If ball doesn't come together, add more water, 1 tbsp. at a time, until it does (it should feel a little dry)."}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. Sprinkle dough with flour if it feels sticky. Repeat folding and feeding, progressing through 2 or 3 successively narrower settings and rolling dough at least twice on each setting, until dough is as thin as you like (fettuccine is usually 1/16-inch thick). If dough sheet gets too long, cut it in half and roll each half separately.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Repeat with remaining 2 dough pieces, setting sheets to the side when done and covering with a kitchen towel (dampened if the weather is dry).'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. Pass each dough sheet, dusted with flour if needed to keep from sticking, through the machine's fettuccine cutter. Lay fettuccine on a baking pan and dust with flour. If it's humid outside, let dry for about 1/2 hour to help keep it from sticking as it cooks."}
{'step_number': 8, 'text': 'To cook, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine and cook until barely tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}

dishes.name: Russian Carrot Salad (Korean-Style)
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Place carrots in a large bowl. Sprinkle garlic over carrots.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Mix vinegar, sugar, and salt together in a small bowl.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in hot oil until soft and translucent, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir coriander and cayenne pepper into the onion; add to carrot mixture and toss. Pour vinegar dressing over carrot mixture; toss to coat.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Transfer carrot salad to a dish with a tight-fitting lid, cover, and refrigerate 4 to 24 hours, tossing salad several times while it marinates.'}

dishes.name: Sunset Magazine’S Irish Oatmeal Bread
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine the first 5 ingredients in the bowl of a stand-up mixer, and let stand 25 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Dissolve granulated sugar and yeast in warm water; let stand 5 minutes or until foamy. Add to oat mixture. Lightly spoon flours into dry measuring cups; level with a knife. Gradually add flour to oat mixture. Beat at medium speed until well blended.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a floured surface. Knead until smooth and elastic (about 8 minutes); add enough of the flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, to prevent dough from sticking to hands (dough will feel sticky).'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Place dough in a large bowl coated with cooking spray, turning to coat top. Cover and let rise in a warm place (85°), free from drafts, 1 hour or until doubled in size. (Gently press two fingers into dough. If indentation remains, dough has risen enough.) Punch dough down; cover and let rest 5 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Divide in half. Working with one portion at a time (cover remaining dough to prevent drying), roll each portion into a 14 x 8-inch rectangle on a floured surface. Roll up each rectangle tightly, starting with a short edge, pressing firmly to eliminate air pockets; pinch seam and ends to seal. Place each loaf, seam sides down, in a 9-inch loaf pan coated with cooking spray. Cover and let rise 30 minutes or until doubled in size.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Preheat oven to 350°. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until loaves are browned on bottom and sound hollow when tapped. Remove from pan, and cool on wire racks.'}

dishes.name: Homemade Roman-Style Pizza Pockets (
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Combine flour, salt, and yeast in large bowl and whisk together until homogenous. Add water and stir with wooden spoon until no dry flour remains, about 2 minutes. Add 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil and stir to incorporate, using hands if necessary to work oil into dough. Transfer dough to a clean large bowl that has been lightly greased with olive oil; cover with plastic wrap, and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Transfer dough to clean surface dusted with flour; dust your hands and dough with flour. Pat dough into large rectangle, with long sides of the rectangle parallel to countertop. Gently pull the upper long edge of the rectangle, stretching dough, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Then gently pull the lower edge, and fold it into the middle of the rectangle. Pinch these folded edges together to seal them together, forming a seam. Rotate dough 90 degrees, and repeat folding and sealing process. Rotate dough 90 degrees and repeat once more. Cover dough with a clean kitchen towel and let rest for 15 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. Lightly drizzle dough with olive oil, and use your hands to gently rub it over the surface. Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 18 hours or up to 3 days.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. Lightly spray 13-by-18-inch rimmed baking sheet with vegetable cooking spray; pour remaining 40g (1.4 ounces; 3 tablespoons) olive oil onto baking sheet and spread over entire inner surface (including rim) with your hands. Transfer dough seam side down to prepared baking sheet, and spread gently with your hands to mostly fill the pan (don't worry if dough doesn't fully stretch to edges). Lightly dust surface of dough with flour, cover with clean kitchen towel, and let rise at room temperature until dough is very soft and puffy and nearly doubled in volume, 1 1/2 to 2 hours."}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). Using floured hands, gently push and stretch dough into corners of the pan by pressing out from the center. Divide dough into 8 equal-sized rectangles by first drizzling olive oil to trace outline of pieces, and then use bench scraper to cut dough along the lines. Drizzle more olive oil over top of the dough, and use hands to gently rub over entire surface. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt. Transfer entire baking sheet with dough to oven, positioning it on top of baking stone.'}

{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Bake until dough is cooked through and top surface of pizza is burnished golden brown, about 16 minutes, rotating baking sheet halfway through baking. Let pizza cool in baking sheet on wire rack for 5 minutes; use spatula to separate pieces. When ready to serve, return pizza pieces to oven to bake directly on baking stone until bottom crust is evenly browned and crisp, about 4 minutes. Transfer to cutting board; cut each piece in half diagonally, and then cut slit down middle of the now-exposed interior of each pizza triangle to form a pizza pocket. Stuff pockets with fillings of your choice, and serve immediately.'}

dishes.name: Arabic Lentil Soup - Shorbat Addas
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large pot or pressure cooker, saute chopped onions in vegetable oil until soft.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Rinse dried lentils several times.'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Add lentils, water, salt and pepper to the pot.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Bring to boil and simmer for an hour or more until lentils turn yellow in color and are soft and dissolving in broth.'}
{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'If using a pressure cooker, cook for 15 minutes after pressure has risen. Release pressure before removing lid.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Whisk lentils to make a smooth soup, or stir to blend for a more textured soup.'}

dishes.name: Lebanese Lentils (Mujadara)
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Heat oil in pan.'}
{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'add onions, and cook on medium high heat until they are brown- stir occasionally.'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'stir in rice and lentils, mix in with onions.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'add water.'}
{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'add salt, mix contents.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'cover and simmer.'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': 'This will take over an hour. The water will be absorbed into rice and lentils. Make sure they are soft. Sometimes you may need to add a little more water. Stir occasionally.'}
{'step_number': 8, 'text': 'Best if served in a shallow bowl, and let sit for 10 minutes or so. Enjoy warm or cold.'}

dishes.name: Korean Style Romaine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Cut romaine crosswise into 2-inch pieces and put in a bowl.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Cook garlic, ginger, and red-pepper flakes in sesame oil in a small heavy skillet over medium-low heat, stirring, until garlic begins to sizzle, about 30 seconds. Stir in soy sauce and water and bring to a boil.'}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Pour hot dressing over romaine and toss to coat. Sprinkle with sesame seeds. Marinate, stirring occasionally, at least 30 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Note:'}
{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Romaine can be made 1 day ahead and chilled. Bring to room temperature before serving.'}

dishes.name: Lentil Patties
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'Cook lentils and when soft, remove from heat and drain. Mash them like doing mashed potatoes and add all the ingredients but the egg.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': 'Let the mixture cool for about 20 minutes and then add the egg beaten, mix well. Form patties the size of the palm of your hand. On a heated skillet with just a drop of olive oil brown them on both sides and that is it. Ouila!'}

dishes.name: Fresh Fettuccine
steps: {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large bowl, mix together flours, salt, cayenne, and black pepper.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. Sprinkle in about 1/3 cup water and work it into flour mixture, then press dough into a rough ball. If ball doesn't come together, add more water, 1 tbsp. at a time, until it does (it should feel a little dry)."}
{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. Sprinkle dough with flour if it feels sticky. Repeat folding and feeding, progressing through 2 or 3 successively narrower settings and rolling dough at least twice on each setting, until dough is as thin as you like (fettuccine is usually 1/16-inch thick). If dough sheet gets too long, cut it in half and roll each half separately.'}
{'step_number': 6, 'text': 'Repeat with remaining 2 dough pieces, setting sheets to the side when done and covering with a kitchen towel (dampened if the weather is dry).'}

{'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. Pass each dough sheet, dusted with flour if needed to keep from sticking, through the machine's fettuccine cutter. Lay fettuccine on a baking pan and dust with flour. If it's humid outside, let dry for about 1/2 hour to help keep it from sticking as it cooks."}
{'step_number': 8, 'text': 'To cook, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine and cook until barely tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}

{'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Repeat this entire folding process once more, for a total of 6 folds. Place dough seam side down in lightly greased large bowl. {'step_number': 4, 'text': "Remove dough from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes. {'step_number': 5, 'text': 'One hour before baking, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position. Place baking stone or Baking Steel on it , and preheat oven to 550°F (290°C). {'step_number': 1, 'text': 'In a large bowl, mix together flours, salt, cayenne, and black pepper.'}

{'step_number': 2, 'text': "Make a well in the center and crack in eggs. Mix them gently but thoroughly into flour by scooping up handfuls and rubbing between your palms. {'step_number': 3, 'text': 'Turn dough out onto a work surface and knead it until fairly smooth and no longer sticky, about 2 minutes.'}

{'step_number': 4, 'text': 'Set a pasta machine to the widest setting. Cut dough into thirds. Working with 1 dough piece at a time (keep others covered with a dampened kitchen towel), pat into a 1/2-in.-thick oval and feed through machine.'}

{'step_number': 5, 'text': 'Fold dough into thirds crosswise and feed through again, starting with an unfolded edge. Fold and feed once more the same way. {'step_number': 7, 'text': "Cut each sheet to about 12 in. long and cover with the towel. {'step_number': 8, 'text': 'To cook, bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add fettuccine and cook until barely tender, about 2 to 3 minutes.'}
{'step_number': 9, 'text': 'Make ahead: Through step 7, up to 2 days, wrapped airtight and chilled; up to 2 months, frozen.'}
